output.headline: Ratifies up to $119,000 for Robert Half to supply contract staff to the Legal Department
output.summary: Robert Half, Inc. of Oakland will provide contract talent services to the district through the Legal Department, as described in the agreement's Exhibit A. The amount is not to exceed $119,000.00 for July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027. The work was scheduled to start before the Board's approval.

output.headline: Accepts $3.72M from the Salesforce Foundation, through Oakland Public Education Fund, for middle schools
output.summary: The district will accept $3,724,125.91 in funding from the Salesforce Foundation, passed through the Oakland Public Education Fund, to support educational outcomes in the district. The grant runs from July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027, and the specific program areas are set out in the agreement.

output.headline: Ratifies $68,887.80 for Star Elevator to fix the elevator pump at Laurel Elementary
output.summary: Star Elevator of Belmont will install a new submersible pump unit on the passenger elevator at Laurel Elementary School to bring it into code compliance. The amount is not to exceed $68,887.80, with work scheduled from July 1 to October 31, 2026. The work was scheduled to start before the Board's approval.

output.headline: Pays Sown to Grow up to $232,900 for a student wellness check-in platform and training in all schools
output.summary: Sown to Grow, Inc. of Oakland will provide its software for weekly student social-emotional check-ins and wellness surveys, along with a social-emotional learning screener and curriculum, teacher and principal training, coaching, and data reports for schools serving grades TK-12. The amount is not to exceed $232,900.00 for August 1, 2026 through June 1, 2027.

output.headline: Ratifies $67,488.10 for Window Tints Everything to add sun-reflecting film at four schools
output.summary: Window Tints Everything of North Hollywood will clean window surfaces and install reflective window film on the south- and west-facing classroom windows most affected by sun at Hoover Elementary, Bridges Academy, Sequoia Elementary and Laurel Elementary. The amount is not to exceed $67,488.10, including a $6,135.31 contingency, with work from July 20 to September 9, 2026. The work was scheduled to start before the Board's approval.

output.headline: Accepts $425,000 from East Bay Community Foundation for Oakland Goes Outdoors staff costs
output.summary: The district will accept a $425,000.00 grant from the East Bay Community Foundation, on behalf of the Robert and Kathryn Riddell Fund, to support district salary and staff expenses at Oakland Goes Outdoors through the Middle Schools Network. The grant covers July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027.

output.headline: Accepts $500,000 from the Association for Continuing Education for Rudsdale High School programs
output.summary: The district will accept a $500,000.00 grant from the Association for Continuing Education to support a learning center program at Rudsdale High School, including workplace learning coordination, four dual enrollment classes, staff training and a student leadership elective. The grant covers July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $45,425.50 for LogicTree's tip-reporting software subscription through June 2029
output.summary: LogicTree IT Solutions, Inc. of Citrus Heights will provide a FormsTrackR subscription for managing tips, expanded to 30 more sites and the staff who receive and assign tips, and will move data over from the district's current HubConnect system. The amount is not to exceed $45,425.50 for July 16, 2026 through June 30, 2029. The work was scheduled to start before the Board's approval.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $77,000 for Yeah, Art! to run after-school music at three middle schools
output.summary: Yeah, Art! of Oakland will provide after-school music instruction for up to 160 students at Melrose, Montera and Westlake Middle Schools, with up to 500 hours of instruction over 30 weeks and up to two student showcases per site. The amount is not to exceed $77,000.00 for August 3, 2026 through June 30, 2027. The work was scheduled to start before the Board's approval.

output.headline: Ratifies $32,007.00 for Peninsulators to add sun-reflecting window film at Chabot Elementary
output.summary: Peninsulators, Inc. of San Jose will prepare window surfaces and install reflective window film on classroom windows most affected by sun at Chabot Elementary School. The lump sum is $32,007.00, including a $2,838.00 contingency, with work from July 30 to September 6, 2026. The work was scheduled to start before the Board's approval.

output.headline: Ratifies $36,200.00 for Peninsulators to add sun-reflecting window film at East Oakland Pride Elementary
output.summary: Peninsulators, Inc. of San Jose will prepare window surfaces and install reflective window film on classroom windows most affected by sun at East Oakland Pride Elementary School. The lump sum is $36,200.00, including a $3,210.00 contingency, with work from July 30 to September 6, 2026. The work was scheduled to start before the Board's approval.

output.headline: Ratifies $20,764.00 for Peninsulators to add sun-reflecting window film at Cleveland Elementary
output.summary: Peninsulators, Inc. of San Jose will prepare window surfaces and install reflective window film on classroom windows most affected by sun at Cleveland Elementary School. The lump sum is $20,764.00, including a $1,887.00 contingency, with work from July 30 to September 6, 2026. The work was scheduled to start before the Board's approval.

output.headline: Ratifies $21,476.00 for Peninsulators to add sun-reflecting window film at Stonehurst Elementary
output.summary: Peninsulators, Inc. of San Jose will prepare window surfaces and install reflective window film on classroom windows most affected by sun at Stonehurst Elementary School. The lump sum is $21,476.00, including a $1,952.00 contingency, with work from July 30 to September 6, 2026. The work was scheduled to start before the Board's approval.

output.headline: Awards $648,295.56 to OBR Electric to replace the Skyline High School field lighting
output.summary: OBR Electric of Oakland was the lowest responsible bidder to install new light poles, underground conduit and foundations, and to test the lighting system for the Skyline High School field. The amount is $648,295.56, including a $120,000.00 contingency, with work expected from August 27 to November 19, 2026. The Board is also rejecting all other bids.

output.headline: Awards $816,100.00 to Redgwick Construction for playground and garden upgrades at Sequoia Elementary
output.summary: Redgwick Construction Company of Oakland was the lowest responsible bidder for site work at Sequoia Elementary School: removing old play structures and asphalt, creating nature and garden spaces with irrigation and drainage, preparing for new play structures, planting trees, and sealing pavement and murals. The amount is $816,100.00, including an $82,400.00 contingency, with work expected from August 27 to October 30, 2026. The Board is also rejecting all other bids.

output.headline: Ratifies the minutes of the Board's August 4, 2026 special meeting
output.summary: The Board is approving the written minutes of its Special Meeting of August 4, 2026, which staff prepared shortly after the meeting. There is no cost.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $40,000 for Prescott Circus Theatre after-school performing arts at two elementary schools
output.summary: Prescott Circus Theatre of Oakland will provide after-school performing arts classes up to two days a week for up to 80 students at Piedmont Avenue and Esperanza Elementary Schools, for a total of 240 hours. The amount is not to exceed $40,000.00 for August 3, 2026 through June 30, 2027. The work was scheduled to start before the Board's approval.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $40,000 for Cantare Con Vivo to run after-school music at three schools
output.summary: Cantare Con Vivo of Oakland will provide music education in after-school programs at Melrose Leadership Academy's Sherman Campus, Horace Mann Elementary and Bridges Academy, reaching up to 100 students with 480 hours of instruction and up to two showcase performances per site. The amount is not to exceed $40,000.00 for August 3, 2026 through June 30, 2027. The work was scheduled to start before the Board's approval.

output.headline: Ratifies $46,900.50 for Climate Pro to add sun-reflecting window film at Horace Mann Elementary
output.summary: Miller Dobbins Family, Inc., doing business as Climate Pro, of Cotati will clean and prepare glass and install reflective window film on 498 classroom windows at Horace Mann Elementary School. The lump sum is $46,900.50, including a $4,139.50 contingency, with work from July 30 to October 6, 2026. The work was scheduled to start before the Board's approval.

output.headline: Pays Elevate Oakland up to $70,000 for music instruction at three middle and high schools
output.summary: Elevate Oakland will provide up to 500 hours of music instruction and performance preparation for up to 90 students at Castlemont High, Oakland Technical High and Elmhurst Middle School, two days a week over 30 weeks. The amount is not to exceed $70,000.00 for August 3, 2026 through June 30, 2027.

output.headline: Accepts $320,000 from Eat.Learn.Play Foundation for food and garden learning at the Central Kitchen
output.summary: The district will accept $320,000.00 from the Eat.Learn.Play Foundation to fund staff capacity and hands-on learning in the Environment, Food and Garden Program at the Central Kitchen and Education Center. The grant period is July 23, 2026 through July 30, 2027.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $58,800 for HERO to run recess and student leadership programs at Allendale Elementary
output.summary: HERO of Oakland will run a structured recess program, support a safe and inclusive playground, and offer student leadership and conflict resolution activities, including a Young HERO leadership program for upper-grade students, at Allendale Elementary School. The amount is not to exceed $58,800.00 for August 10, 2026 through May 25, 2027. The work was scheduled to start before the Board's approval.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $60,000 for Oakland Symphony after-school music classes at five elementary schools
schools: Martin Luther King, Jr. Elementary School
output.sourceIssueCandidate: The item title says 2026-2027, but the action text calls the agreement a "Services Agreement 2025-2026" while giving a term of August 3, 2026 through June 30, 2027.
output.summary: Oakland Symphony will teach music classes during the after-school program at Hoover, Garfield, Manzanita SEED, Brookfield and Martin Luther King, Jr. Elementary Schools, two days a week for 30 weeks, for up to 160 students and at least 432 hours. The amount is not to exceed $60,000.00 for August 3, 2026 through June 30, 2027. The work was scheduled to start before the Board's approval.

output.headline: Ratifies an $800 membership fee to the Bay Area Collaborative for special education planning services
output.summary: This memorandum of understanding (MOU) sets a fee, not to exceed $800.00, to be paid by the Special Education Local Plan Area for membership in the Bay Area Collaborative, which supports the services of the planning areas that chair the group. It covers July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027. The work was scheduled to start before the Board's approval.

output.headline: Pays Urban Heat Academy up to $150,000 for after-school stepping and cultural arts at four schools
output.summary: Urban Heat Academy of Alameda will provide after-school stepping and cultural arts classes, covering rhythm, movement, choreography, teamwork and leadership, for an estimated 25 to 30 students per site at four school sites, for 864 hours in total. The amount is not to exceed $150,000.00 for August 27, 2026 through May 31, 2027.

output.headline: Pays EliteGamingLIVE up to $237,709.49 for an online esports learning hub at 17 middle schools
output.summary: EliteGamingLIVE, Inc. of Columbia, Maryland will provide an online hub where students build gaming skills, explore esports career pathways and use education resources, serving 17 middle school campuses across three seasons with about 3,060 student participation opportunities. The amount is not to exceed $237,709.49 for August 26, 2026 through May 31, 2027.

output.headline: Amends Star Academy's 2026-27 special education contract to change class size, calendar and report terms
output.summary: This amendment changes three sections of the district's nonpublic school and agency master contract with Star Academy of San Rafael: class size, calendars, and student progress reports and assessments. Star Academy provides special education services required by a student's Individualized Education Program for July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027. All other terms stay in effect, and no dollar amount is stated.

output.headline: Ratifies a no-cost agreement for Eagle Ambulance to give students emergency medical ride-alongs
output.summary: Eagle Ambulance of San Leandro will provide ride-along experiences for students in the Highway to Work: Emergency Medical Technician program, through the High School Linked Learning Office, at no cost to the district. It covers July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027. The work was scheduled to start before the Board's approval.

output.headline: Approves $1,372,113 in Measure G1 carryover funds for named schools
output.summary: The Board is adopting a resolution that follows the Measure G1 oversight commission's recommendation to approve a carryover allocation of $1,372,113 for named schools from the 2025-2026 school year. Carryover means money not spent last year that is allowed to be used again. Measure G1 is the local parcel tax for teacher retention and middle school improvement.

output.headline: Authorizes demolition of obsolete portable buildings at the former John Swett and Tilden campus
output.summary: This resolution authorizes the demolition of obsolete portable buildings and site stabilization at the former John Swett Elementary and Tilden Child Development Center campus, in support of the Facilities Master Plan and the district's asset management strategy. No dollar amount is stated.

output.headline: Pays a consultant up to $15,600 for Board facilitation and governance support

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $15,600.00

output.summary: The district is hiring an individual contractor from Alameda to facilitate meetings, develop leadership skills and give governance support to the Board of Education. The agreement runs from June 1, 2026, through February 1, 2027, and costs no more than $15,600. The service period began before the Board's vote.

output.headline: Approves the minutes of the Board's August 12, 2026 regular meeting
output.summary: The Board is formally approving the written record of its August 12, 2026 regular meeting. Staff prepared the minutes shortly after the meeting. No money is involved.

output.headline: Approves amended 2026-27 Measure G1 funding applications for named schools
output.summary: The Board is adopting a resolution that follows the Measure G1 oversight commission's recommendation to approve amended 2026-2027 school year funding applications for named schools. Measure G1 is the local parcel tax for teacher retention and middle school improvement. The text does not state a dollar amount or list the schools.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $114,000 a year for Olson Remcho Law Firm legal advice through June 2028
output.summary: This memorandum of understanding and engagement policy lets the General Counsel's office retain Olson Remcho Law Firm for advice on the Teacher Retention and Educational Programs Replacement Act, plus elections, campaign finance, ethics, public policy and litigation defense as needed. The amount is not to exceed $114,000 in a fiscal year, for July 20, 2026 through June 30, 2028. The work was scheduled to start before the Board's approval.
